template_info.name: PDBmdAuto Full 265915
template_info.description: Automated 11-node MD preparation pipeline: PDB fetch, homology modeling (ProMod3), protonation, GROMACS topology, solvation, vacuum & solvated relaxation, and production MD. Demo: protein 4Z8J (SNX27 PDZ + PTHR peptide, 2 chains, 5 missing residues).
template_info.author: Boundary Computing

options.name: PDB FASTA Parser
options.description: Parse PDB structures and extract FASTA sequences using BioPython. Supports RCSB PDB API fetching by ID and local file processing with chain splitting, HETATM handling, and missing residues analysis.

options.doc:
Parse PDB structures and extract FASTA sequences using BioPython.

    Supports two modes:
    - **PDB ID mode**: Fetch PDB + FASTA from RCSB by ID (e.g. "3LZ0")
    - **Local file mode**: Process a local PDB file

    Features:
    - Automatic chain splitting into individual FASTA files
    - HETATM record handling (ligands, modified residues)
    - Missing residues extraction from PDB header
    - Protein and DNA/RNA residue support

    Input: Optional predecessor data (case_name, working_path)
    Output: FASTA file(s), optional missing residues CSV

input_mode.label: Input Mode
input_mode.docstring: 'pdb_id' to fetch from RCSB API, 'local_file' for a local PDB.

pdb_id.docstring: 4-character RCSB PDB identifier (e.g. '3LZ0'). Used in pdb_id mode.

pdb_file.label: PDB File
pdb_file.docstring: Path to a local PDB file. Used in local_file mode.

case_name.label: Case Name
case_name.docstring: Identifier for this case. Falls back to PDB ID, predecessor data, or 'protein'.

output_dir.docstring: Directory where output files will be written.

split_chains.label: Split by Chain
split_chains.docstring: Create separate FASTA files for each chain.

include_hetatm.label: Include HETATM
include_hetatm.docstring: Include HETATM records (ligands, modified residues) in sequence extraction.

check_pdb_header.label: Check PDB Header
check_pdb_header.docstring: Extract missing residues information from the PDB header.

force_to_run.docstring: Execute regardless of previous results. When enabled, the node will always run even if the configuration hasn't changed.

options.name: Generate Alignment
options.description: Generate alignment files for homology modeling from PDB structure and FASTA sequences
options.doc:
Generate per-chain alignment files for homology modeling.

    Reads a PDB structure and missing residues information (from predecessor
    pdb_fasta_biopython node or PDB header) and generates:
    - .seq files: raw FASTA alignment per chain
    - .ali files: template/target alignment pairs for ProMod3 or MODELLER

    The template entry shows the existing structure with '-' at missing
    positions. The target entry shows the complete sequence.

    Input: predecessor data from pdb_fasta_biopython (PDB file, chain info,
           optional missing residues CSVs, optional FASTA files)
    Output: Per-chain .seq and .ali files in chain-specific subdirectories

options.name: Multi-Chain Alignment
options.description: Merge per-chain alignment files into a single multi-chain alignment for homology modeling
options.doc:
Merge per-chain alignment files into a single multi-chain alignment.

    Reads per-chain .ali files produced by gen_ali and merges them into
    a single alignment file for multi-chain homology modeling with
    ProMod3 or MODELLER.

    Features:
    - Chain selection (all or specific chains)
    - DNA/RNA masking with '.' characters (MODELLER convention)
    - '/' chain separators between chains
    - Proper protein chain range in header

    Input: predecessor data from gen_ali (per-chain .ali files, chain info)
    Output: Single merged .ali file in Merge/ subdirectory

merge_folder_name.docstring: Subfolder name for the merged alignment file.

options.name: Merge PDB Chains
options.description: Merge selected PDB chains into a single structure file for homology modeling
options.doc:
Merge selected PDB chains into a single structure file.

    Reads chain information from predecessor (gen_multi_chain_ali) and
    extracts the selected chains from the original PDB file into a
    merged PDB. DNA/RNA chains are written with HETATM records
    (MODELLER/ProMod3 convention).

    Output files (in Merge/ subdirectory):
    - merge.pdb: Merged structure with selected chains
    - {case}_chain_type.json: Chain type mapping (P1/DL)
    - {case}_chain_name.json: Selected chain IDs list

    Input: predecessor data (working_path, chain_types, pdb_chain_list)
    Output: Merged PDB file path and chain metadata

case_name.docstring: Case identifier. Leave empty to use predecessor data.

merge_folder_name.docstring: Subfolder name for merged output files.

merge_file_name.docstring: Output filename for the merged PDB.

options.name: Fix Missing Residues
options.description: Fix missing residues in PDB structures using ProMod3 homology modeling engine
options.doc:
Fix missing residues in PDB structures using ProMod3.

    Uses the ProMod3 homology modeling engine (SWISS-MODEL) to fill
    gaps in protein structures. ProMod3 searches a fragment database
    (~19.7M fragments), performs loop modeling, rebuilds sidechains,
    and runs energy minimization.

    Requires:
    - ProMod3 installed (`pixi add promod3` from bioconda channel)
    - Per-chain .ali alignment files (from gen_ali)
    - Merged PDB structure (from merge_pdb_chains)

    Only protein chains are modeled — DNA/RNA chains are preserved as-is.

    Input: predecessor data (working_path, output_pdb, chain_types)
    Output: Repaired PDB file in Merge/ subdirectory

case_name.docstring: Case identifier. Leave empty to use predecessor data.

model_termini.docstring: If true, also model terminal extensions (N/C-terminal residues beyond the template).

options.name: pKa + GROMACS EM
options.description: pH-dependent protonation (PDB2PQR/PROPKA) + GROMACS topology (pdb2gmx) + two-step vacuum energy minimisation
options.doc:
Protonation prediction + GROMACS topology + energy minimisation.

    Takes a PDB file (typically from fix_residues or merge step) and:
    1. Predicts protonation states via PDB2PQR/PROPKA at target pH
    2. Bridges PQR → PDB by renaming titratable residues (HID/HIE/HIP, ASH, GLH, CYX)
    3. Generates GROMACS topology via pdb2gmx -ignh on the patched PDB
    4. Creates triclinic simulation box with padding
    5. Runs two-step energy minimisation (unconstrained → h-bonds)

    Output: Energy-minimised GRO + topology TOP ready for solvation.

case_name.label: Case Name
case_name.docstring: Leave empty to use predecessor data.

input_pdb.label: Input PDB File
input_pdb.docstring: PDB from fix_residues. Leave empty: auto-discovers Merge/fixed.pdb from predecessor working_path.

output_dir.label: Output Directory
output_dir.docstring: GROMACS working folder. Leave empty: creates gmx/ in case folder. All downstream nodes share this folder.

force_field.label: Force Field
force_field.docstring: GROMACS force field. PDB2PQR uses matching naming: AMBER (HID/HIE/HIP) for amber*, CHARMM (HSD/HSE/HSP) for charmm*.

box_distance.label: Box Distance (nm)
box_distance.docstring: Padding distance around solute for simulation box.

em_steps.label: EM Steps
em_steps.docstring: Maximum steps per EM stage (2 stages total).

ph.label: pH
ph.docstring: Target pH for PROPKA protonation state prediction.

run_pdb2pqr.label: Run PDB2PQR
run_pdb2pqr.docstring: Run PDB2PQR/PROPKA for pH-dependent protonation. If disabled, pdb2gmx uses its own hydrogen-bond analysis.

force_to_run.docstring: Execute regardless of previous results. When enabled, the node will always run even if the configuration hasn't changed.

options.name: Original Atom Groups
options.description: Build GROMACS index groups (OriHeavy, OriBackBone) for original vs homology-modeled residues
options.doc:
Generate custom GROMACS index groups for position restraints.

    Creates OriHeavy (all heavy atoms from original residues) and
    OriBackBone (backbone atoms from original residues) groups.
    Used by gmx_md_relax (full_4step) with freezegrps for vacuum relaxation.

    Runs after pka_gmx_em, before gmx_md_relax and solvation.

input_structure.docstring: Vacuum structure from pka_gmx_em. Leave empty: auto-discovers pdb2gmx.gro.

options.name: GMX MD Relaxation
options.description: GROMACS multi-step relaxation — energy minimization and NVT equilibration
options.doc:
GROMACS relaxation/equilibration with protocol selector.

    Protocols:
    - full_4step (default): 4-step progressive unfreezing protocol from legacy pdbmdauto.
      Uses OriHeavy/OriBackBone freezegrps to first equilibrate water/ions around the
      rigid protein, then progressively release constraints. Essential for systems with
      homology-modeled missing residues.
    - em_only: Single energy minimization (steepest descent). Quick for testing.
    - custom: Single grompp+mdrun with user-provided MDP file.

case_name.label: Case Name
case_name.docstring: Leave empty to use predecessor data.

protocol.label: Relaxation Protocol
protocol.docstring: full_4step: 4-step progressive unfreezing (NVT frozen→NVT backbone→CG EM×2). em_only: single steepest-descent EM. custom: single step with user MDP.

input_top_file.docstring: Topology. Leave empty: auto-discovers from predecessor.

input_gro_file.docstring: Solvated structure. Leave empty: auto-discovers from predecessor.

input_ndx_file.docstring: Index file with OriHeavy/OriBackBone groups. Leave empty: auto-discovers.

options.name: GMX Solvate & Ionize
options.description: GROMACS solvation and ionization — add water box and neutralize with ions
options.doc:
GROMACS solvation and ionization.

    If connected to a predecessor (e.g., fix_residues_promod3 or pdb2pqr),
    auto-discovers the PDB/PQR file and runs pdb2gmx to generate GRO + TOP.
    Then sets up box, adds water, neutralizes with ions.

    Includes a bundled ions.mdp for genion preprocessing. Users can override
    with their own MDP file.

options.doc:
Simple GROMACS MD simulation node for local execution.

    This is a Level 2 wrapper that:
    1. Extracts parameters from BoCoFlow UI
    2. Resolves file paths
    3. Calls core functions (Level 1)
    4. Formats results for BoCoFlow

    The actual GROMACS execution logic is in core.py and can be
    tested independently without BoCoFlow dependencies.
